metaData.originalTitle: 京东健康 OPC 团队的产品全流程 Skill 探索
metaData.title: JD Health OPC Team's Exploration of Full-Cycle Product Skills
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Drawing on Anthropic's Product Management Skills, the JD Health OPC team breaks down the full product cycle into four stages: problem assessment, requirement definition, sprint execution, and post-launch review, providing reusable prompt templates and material input specifications.
metaData.summary: The article details how the JD Health OPC (One Person Company) team adapted Anthropic's open-source 8 Product Management Skills (synthesize-research, metrics-review, competitive-brief, product-brainstorming, write-spec, roadmap-update, sprint-planning, stakeholder-update) to enhance their product workflow. The author notes that in an OPC team without dedicated product roles, this set of Skills provides a "shared product-engineering decision-making framework" that standardizes the process from requirement emergence to launch. The article unfolds across four stages: the first stage uses synthesize-research and metrics-review to determine if a problem is worth solving; the second stage uses product-brainstorming to diverge on solutions and write-spec to converge on requirement specifications; the third stage uses roadmap-update to determine priorities and sprint-planning to implement the iteration plan; the fourth stage uses metrics-review to review metrics and stakeholder-update to sync with different audiences. The article also provides a 5-field format for material input, prompt templates for each stage, a roadmap change description template, common pitfalls, and a minimal starting path.

mainPoints.point: When an OPC team lacks dedicated product roles, Anthropic PM Skills can carry product judgment and workflow.
mainPoints.explanation: Mapping the 8 Skills to the four stages of problem assessment, requirement definition, sprint execution, and post-launch review forms a reusable, lightweight working protocol.

mainPoints.point: Before entering requirement definition, problem assessment must be done first rather than directly writing a PRD.
mainPoints.explanation: Using synthesize-research and metrics-review to determine if a problem is worth solving avoids wasting resources on the wrong requirements.

mainPoints.point: Before materials enter a Skill, they must be formatted according to five fields: source, time, subject, content, and association.
mainPoints.explanation: Indiscriminately feeding materials to AI reduces output confidence; formatted input is a prerequisite for ensuring analysis quality.

mainPoints.point: Iteration plans should only allocate 70%-80% capacity, reserving a buffer for online issues and ad-hoc collaboration.
mainPoints.explanation: 100% capacity planning leaves the team unable to handle uncertainty; reasonable buffering ensures sustainable delivery.

keyQuotes: Any requirement, once it enters development, must go through at least six stages: 'evidence, hypothesis, scope, schedule, acceptance, and review'.
Adding a new requirement is not 'doing a little more', but a reallocation of resources.

relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: JD.com's self-developed database kernel, DongSQL V1.2.0, is officially released, achieving significant performance breakthroughs in core dimensions such as hot row update, master-slave replication, execution plan caching, massive table startup, and SIMD acceleration, providing a more solid technical foundation for retail scenarios.

relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the OpenAI Codex team's "pirate ship" operating model, revealing their minimalist spec documentation, AI-driven development workflow, and the fundamental shift in the product manager role in the AGI era.

relatedArticles.title: Detailed Explanation of OpenClaw Agent and Skill Architecture
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core architecture of JD.com's open-source OpenClaw Agent framework, focusing on its Agent execution engine, Skill knowledge injection mechanism, Master-Subagent collaboration model, and multi-layer fault tolerance system, aiming to address challenges faced by AI Agents in production environments such as multi-channel integration, long-term operation, and flexible knowledge expansion.

relatedArticles.title: B-Side Order Storage Architecture Upgrade: JD.com's Technical Evolution in Tackling High-Concurrency Pressure on ES
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details JD.com's systematic technical evolution of its B-side POP order ES storage architecture, addressing core pain points such as data skew, oversized shards, frequent updates, and high maintenance costs through a combined solution involving tenant isolation, double-layer hash routing, differentiated sharding, and automated archiving.

relatedArticles.title: EP20 Review of AI Content Production Part 1: Does AI Know What You Want? · Case
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Hosts Hanyang, Keda, and Zhongqing review the prerequisites for AI content creation, revealing that before AI can be involved in production, the team must first clarify and reach a consensus on 'what good content looks like' through hand-written samples. This step is more critical and challenging than the AI technology itself.

relatedArticles.title: Dialogue with Singularity AI: The Next Generation of AI Hardware for Kids is Not a Chatbot, but a Self-Evolving Physical Agent
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This in-depth interview with the founder of Singularity AI elaborates on how their children's AI hardware product 'Duoqi' uses software-hardware decoupling, AI Coding, and scenario script accumulation to create a self-evolving physical agent, rather than a simple chatbot.
